summary: A gateway OpenTelemetry Collector (contrib 0.165.0) on EKS (two t3.large nodes) takes 60 spans a second from telemetrygen v0.165.0 as single-span OTLP requests (--batch=false, 4 workers at 15 spans a second; each trace is a parent and its default one child span, and each worker logs how many traces it generated) and exports them over OTLP to a relay Collector, which forwards them to the Splunk OTel Collector agent (chart 0.163.1) and on to Splunk Observability Cloud. Scaling the relay to 0 for 30 s, from 10 s into each 50 s load, is the outage; all three configs cap the exporter's retry interval at 5 s so the drain is comparable. Three gateway configs, one change at a time: batch.yaml (batch processor with defaults, default sending_queue of 1000 requests), migrated.yaml (the OpenTelemetry blog's one-line migration: no batch processor, sending_queue batch enabled, queue defaults), sized.yaml (migrated plus sizer items and queue_size 100000). Runs batch-1, migrated-1, batch-2, migrated-2 (reproduce.sh) and sized-1, sized-2 (fix.sh); the gateway restarts for each. Measured per run: spans the sender generated (2 x its trace count), and from the gateway's own metrics spans accepted and refused (attempts) by its receiver, spans its exporter failed to enqueue, spans sent, spans lost (generated minus sent), queue peak and capacity read every 2 s, and the accept rate between 2 s and 10 s into the load, and seconds from the relay's return until the queue, read every 2 s, is back at its pre-outage level for 3 reads in a row (from the relay's scale-up command), and whether the drain completed; fix.sh also reads, for all six runs, Splunk APM's spans.count for the load service from each run's load start to 20 s after its drain (runs at least 30 s apart).
expected: reproduce.sh: the gateway's exporter fails to enqueue no span in batch-1 and batch-2, and fails to enqueue spans in migrated-1 and migrated-2 (enqueue failed > 0), then HERO_RESULT: reproduced. fix.sh: in sized-1 and sized-2 the exporter enqueues every span, the receiver refuses nothing, and the gateway sends every span the sender generated (lost <= 0), with a complete drain, then HERO_RESULT: fixed. Refused attempts, spans lost in the other runs, queue peak, capacity, seconds to drain and Splunk APM span counts are measured results, not conditions.

# Batch processor deprecated? Move batching to sending_queue, measured through a 30 s outage

The OpenTelemetry Collector's `batch` processor is deprecated. The migration in the OpenTelemetry blog is one line: remove
the processor and turn on batching in the exporter's `sending_queue`. The blog also warns that the queue then holds smaller,
unbatched requests, so the same `queue_size` can hold much less data. This lab measures what that means for spans when the
gateway's export target goes away for 30 seconds.

## What runs

- EKS 1.34 with two t3.large nodes (public subnets, no NAT), the Splunk OTel Collector chart 0.163.1 as the agent.
- A gateway Collector (contrib 0.165.0) that exports over OTLP to a relay Collector (contrib 0.165.0), which forwards to
  the Splunk agent on its node. Scaling the relay to 0 is the outage.
- telemetrygen v0.165.0 sending 60 spans a second as single-span requests (`--batch=false`), like many small clients. Each trace is a
  parent and one child span (telemetrygen's default), and its rate limit counts spans. Each worker logs how many traces it
  generated, so the sender's own count is 2 spans a trace; `check.sh` confirms the gateway accepts exactly that many when
  nothing is refused or dropped.

Six runs, one change at a time (the gateway restarts for each):

| Runs | Gateway config |
| --- | --- |
| batch-1, batch-2 | `batch` processor with its defaults, default `sending_queue` |
| migrated-1, migrated-2 | no `batch` processor, `sending_queue: { batch: { enabled: true } }`, queue left at its defaults |
| sized-1, sized-2 | the migrated config with `sizer: items` and `queue_size: 100000` |

Each run: 50 s of load, the relay down from 10 s to 40 s, then up to 60 s for the queue to drain. All three configs cap the
exporter's retry interval at 5 s (`retry_on_failure.max_interval`, default 30 s), so the drain isn't measured against a long
backoff. With the default, a drain can take longer than measured here. Counts: spans the sender generated, and from the gateway's own metrics, spans accepted and refused by its receiver
(refused counts attempts, since the sender retries), spans its exporter couldn't enqueue, spans sent, and its queue size
against capacity, read every 2 s, with accepted and sent. From those reads: the accept rate before the outage, and the
seconds from the relay's return until the queue is back at its pre-outage level. Lost = generated minus sent. `fix.sh` then reads, for all six runs, how many spans Splunk
APM holds for the load service from the run's load start to 20 s after its drain; runs are at least 30 s apart.

## Run it in your own account

Export `SPLUNK_REALM`, `SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN` (ingest) and `SPLUNK_API_TOKEN` (read), and `AWS_REGION` and `LAB_NAME`, then:

```bash
terraform init && terraform apply
./reproduce.sh
./fix.sh
./cleanup.sh && terraform destroy
```

`check.sh` runs the same configs, load and stats script in Docker, with no AWS account and no Splunk tokens.

## Limits

One load shape (many small requests), one outage length and one queue size per config. A persistent queue
(`file_storage`) is a separate change and isn't measured here.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The free check, on a GitHub runner with Docker, before AWS is paid for. It runs the lab's real parts: the gateway image
# with all three real configs from k8s/30-gateway.yaml, the relay's real config, the real telemetrygen image and flags from
# k8s/20-load.yaml, and the real stats script. Only the relay's exporter changes: it writes to a file instead of the
# Splunk agent. Each config gets a short version of a run: 30 s of load, the relay stopped for 15 s from 5 s in.
# It proves, before AWS: every config is valid on contrib 0.165.0, telemetrygen takes the lab's flags and sends single-span
# requests of 2 spans a trace (checked against the gateway), the stats script reads the receiver, exporter and queue metrics, and the relay passes spans on once it's back.
# What each config refuses or drops is printed, not asserted: that is the lab's finding.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
mkdir -p c/conf c/stats c/out
chmod 777 c/out

python3 - <<'PY'
import re
def block(path, key):
    text = open(path).read()
    m = re.search(rf"^  {re.escape(key)}: \|\n((?:    .*\n|\n)+)", text, re.M)
    return "\n".join(line[4:] for line in m[1].splitlines()) + "\n"
for k in ("batch.yaml", "migrated.yaml", "sized.yaml"):
    conf = block("k8s/30-gateway.yaml", k)
    assert "endpoint: http://relay:4318" in conf, k
    open(f"c/conf/{k}", "w").write(conf)
relay = block("k8s/30-gateway.yaml", "relay.yaml")
open("c/conf/relay-real.yaml", "w").write(relay)
# The one change from the cluster: the relay writes what it would send to the Splunk agent into a file.
relay = relay.replace("otlphttp:\n    endpoint: http://${env:HOST_IP}:4318", "file:\n    path: /out/spans.json")
relay = relay.replace("exporters: [otlphttp]", "exporters: [file]")
assert "otlphttp" not in relay and "/out/spans.json" in relay
open("c/conf/relay.yaml", "w").write(relay)
open("c/stats/gwstats.py", "w").write(block("k8s/30-gateway.yaml", "gwstats.py"))
load = open("k8s/20-load.yaml").read()
args = re.findall(r"^        - (.+)$", load, re.M)
assert args[0] == "traces" and "--batch=false" in args and not any(a.startswith("--child-spans") for a in args), args
args = [a.replace("gateway.demo.svc.cluster.local", "gateway").replace("--duration=50s", "--duration=30s")
         .replace("LAB_ENV", "check").replace('"RUN"', '"check"') for a in args]
open("c/load-args.txt", "w").write("\n".join(args) + "\n")
PY
GATEWAY=$(grep -m1 -oE 'otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:[0-9.]+' k8s/30-gateway.yaml)
LOADGEN=$(grep -m1 -oE 'ghcr.io/[^ ]+telemetrygen:v[0-9.]+' k8s/20-load.yaml)
PY=$(grep -m1 -oE 'python:[^ "]+' k8s/30-gateway.yaml)
for img in "$GATEWAY" "$LOADGEN" "$PY"; do
  for i in 1 2 3; do docker pull -q "$img" >/dev/null && break; sleep 10; done
done
fail() { echo "CHECK FAILED: $*"; exit 1; }

echo "== Every config is valid on $GATEWAY"
for k in batch.yaml migrated.yaml sized.yaml relay-real.yaml relay.yaml; do
  docker run --rm -e HOST_IP=127.0.0.1 -v "$PWD/c/conf:/conf:ro" "$GATEWAY" validate "--config=/conf/$k" || fail "$k is not valid"
  echo "valid: $k"
done
docker network create lab >/dev/null

run() {   # config
  local cfg=$1
  echo "== ${cfg%.yaml}: 30 s of load, the relay stopped from 5 s to 20 s"
  rm -f c/out/spans.json
  docker rm -f gateway relay load >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  docker run -d --name relay --network lab -v "$PWD/c/conf:/conf:ro" -v "$PWD/c/out:/out" "$GATEWAY" --config=/conf/relay.yaml >/dev/null
  docker run -d --name gateway --network lab -v "$PWD/c/conf:/conf:ro" "$GATEWAY" "--config=/conf/$cfg" >/dev/null
  for n in gateway relay; do
    for i in $(seq 1 30); do docker logs "$n" 2>&1 | grep -q 'Everything is ready' && break; sleep 1; done
    docker logs "$n" 2>&1 | grep -q 'Everything is ready' || { docker logs "$n" 2>&1 | tail -20; fail "$n didn't start with $cfg"; }
  done
  docker run -d --name load --network lab "$LOADGEN" $(tr '\n' ' ' < c/load-args.txt) >/dev/null
  sleep 5
  docker stop -t 2 relay >/dev/null
  local peak=0 cap=0 q
  for i in $(seq 1 7); do
    q=$(docker run --rm --network lab -v "$PWD/c/stats:/stats:ro" "$PY" python /stats/gwstats.py | sed -n 's/^GW queue_size=//p;s/^GW queue_capacity=/C /p' | tr '\n' ' ')
    set -- $q; [ "${1%.*}" -gt "$peak" ] && peak=${1%.*}; cap=${3:-0}
    sleep 1
  done
  docker start relay >/dev/null
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' load 2>/dev/null)" = true ] || break; sleep 1; done
  sleep 15   # the drain
  docker run --rm --network lab -v "$PWD/c/stats:/stats:ro" "$PY" python /stats/gwstats.py | tee "c/gw-${cfg%.yaml}.txt"
  docker logs load > "c/load-${cfg%.yaml}.txt" 2>&1
  echo "load log: $(grep 'traces generated' "c/load-${cfg%.yaml}.txt" | cut -c1-160 | tr '\n' ' ')"
  local relayed; relayed=$(python3 -c "
import json; n=0
for l in open('c/out/spans.json'):
    for rs in json.loads(l).get('resourceSpans', []):
        for ss in rs.get('scopeSpans', []): n += len(ss.get('spans', []))
print(n)" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  echo "CHECK ${cfg%.yaml}: queue peak $peak of capacity $cap; spans the relay wrote after it was back: $relayed"
  echo "$peak $cap $relayed" > "c/result-${cfg%.yaml}.txt"
  docker rm -f load gateway relay >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

for cfg in batch.yaml migrated.yaml sized.yaml; do run "$cfg"; done
for r in batch migrated sized; do
  read -r peak cap relayed < "c/result-$r.txt"
  grep -q '^GW accepted=[1-9]' "c/gw-$r.txt" || fail "$r: the stats script read no accepted spans"
  grep -q '^GW queue_capacity=[1-9]' "c/gw-$r.txt" || fail "$r: the stats script read no queue capacity"
  grep -q '^GW sent=[1-9]' "c/gw-$r.txt" || fail "$r: the gateway sent nothing after the relay came back"
  [ "$relayed" -gt 0 ] || fail "$r: the relay wrote no spans"
  [ "$(grep -c 'traces generated' "c/load-$r.txt")" = 4 ] || fail "$r: telemetrygen did not log a count for each of its 4 workers"
  gen=$(grep 'traces generated' "c/load-$r.txt" | grep -oE '"traces": ?[0-9]+|traces=[0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+$' | awk '{t += 2 * $1} END {print t + 0}')
  [ "$gen" -gt 0 ] || fail "$r: could not read the sender's count"
  # The lab counts 2 spans a trace (a parent and telemetrygen's default one child). With nothing refused or dropped, the
  # gateway must have accepted exactly that many, which proves the factor.
  if grep -q '^GW refused=0$' "c/gw-$r.txt" && grep -q '^GW enqueue_failed=0$' "c/gw-$r.txt"; then
    grep -q "^GW accepted=$gen\$" "c/gw-$r.txt" || fail "$r: the gateway accepted $(sed -n 's/^GW accepted=//p' "c/gw-$r.txt") spans, not 2 x traces = $gen"
  fi
  echo "$r: generated $gen; $(grep -E '^GW (accepted|refused|enqueue_failed|sent|send_failed|queue_capacity)=' "c/gw-$r.txt" | tr '\n' ' ') (printed, not asserted)"
done
echo "CHECK PASSED"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Never fail hard. Nothing here creates AWS resources outside Terraform.
set +e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
name=$(terraform output -raw cluster_name 2>/dev/null)
if [ -n "$name" ]; then
  aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$name" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null 2>&1
  if kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 180 helm uninstall splunk-otel-collector -n splunk --timeout 120s >/dev/null 2>&1
    timeout 120 kubectl delete namespace demo splunk --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1
    echo "cleanup: helm release uninstalled, namespaces deleting"
  else
    echo "cleanup: cluster not reachable, nothing to remove"
  fi
else
  echo "cleanup: no cluster output, nothing to remove"
fi
exit 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# THE FIX: keep the migration (no batch processor, sending_queue batch enabled) and size the queue in items, as the
# OpenTelemetry blog suggests: sizer items, queue_size 100000. Runs sized-1 and sized-2 under the same load and outage, then
# reads from Splunk APM how many spans of the load service it holds for each of the six runs.
# Fixed when, in both sized runs, the exporter enqueues every span, the receiver refuses nothing, and the gateway sends every
# span the sender generated, with a complete drain.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh
. ./splunk.sh

start_clock 820 not_fixed

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
APP_NODE=$(cat app-node.txt); LOAD_NODE=$(cat load-node.txt)
[ -s results.txt ] || fail "reproduce.sh left no results"

echo "== The sized config's queue"
kubectl -n demo get configmap gateway -o jsonpath='{.data.sized\.yaml}' | sed -n '/^exporters/,/^service/p' | sed 's/^/  sized.yaml | /'

for r in sized-1 sized-2; do
  echo "== Run $r: sized.yaml, 50 s of load, the relay down from 10 s to 40 s"
  start_run "$r" 120
  outage_run "$r"
  measures "$r"
done

echo "== Summary, all six runs"
summary

echo "== Spans Splunk APM holds for the load service, per run window (read once, after a wait for APM)"
sleep "$(cap 90 240)"
for r in batch-1 migrated-1 batch-2 migrated-2 sized-1 sized-2; do
  n=$(apm_spans "$r")
  echo "$r: Splunk APM spans.count for checkout-load from load start to 20 s after the drain: $n (the sender generated $(col "$r" 2), the gateway sent $(col "$r" 6))"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: splunk_apm_spans[$r]=$n"
  [ "$(remaining)" -gt 30 ] || { echo "note: out of time for the remaining Splunk reads"; break; }
done

ok=1
for r in sized-1 sized-2; do
  [ "$(col "$r" 5)" = 0 ] || ok=0
  [ "$(col "$r" 4)" = 0 ] || ok=0
  [ "$(col "$r" 7)" -le 0 ] || ok=0
  [ "$(col "$r" 12)" = 1 ] || ok=0
done
[ "$ok" = 1 ] && emit fixed || emit not_fixed

# The load: telemetrygen v0.165.0 sends 60 spans a second (4 workers at 15 each; its rate limit counts spans) for 50 s, one
# span per OTLP request (--batch=false). Each trace is a parent and one child span (its default --child-spans=1), like many pods or short-lived clients sending small requests to one gateway. Every span carries the
# run's label. Each worker logs how many traces it generated; 2 spans each is the sender's own count. --allow-export-failures keeps it sending when the gateway refuses a request.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: load
  namespace: demo
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: LOAD_NODE
  enableServiceLinks: false
  containers:
    - name: load
      image: ghcr.io/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/telemetrygen:v0.165.0
      args:
        - traces
        - --otlp-http
        - --otlp-endpoint=gateway.demo.svc.cluster.local:4318
        - --otlp-insecure
        - --batch=false
        - --workers=4
        - --rate=15
        - --duration=50s
        - --service=checkout-load
        - --allow-export-failures
        - --otlp-attributes=deployment.environment="LAB_ENV"
        - --telemetry-attributes=lab.run="RUN"
      resources:
        requests: { cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi }

# The gateway: the upstream OpenTelemetry Collector (contrib 0.165.0). The load sends it traces; it exports them over OTLP
# to the relay, which forwards them to the Splunk OTel Collector agent on its node, which sends to Splunk Observability
# Cloud. Scaling the relay to 0 is the outage: the gateway's export target is gone, so its sending queue fills.
# Three configs, and CONFIG picks one. All three cap the exporter's retry interval at 5 s (default 30 s), so the drain after
# the outage is measured without waiting on a long backoff. Each run changes one thing from the one before:
#   batch.yaml     the batch processor with its defaults, and the exporter's default sending_queue (1000 requests)
#   migrated.yaml  the one-line migration from the OpenTelemetry blog: no batch processor, sending_queue batch enabled;
#                  the queue keeps its defaults
#   sized.yaml     migrated.yaml, with the queue sized in items: sizer items, queue_size 100000
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: demo
data:
  batch.yaml: |
    receivers:
      otlp:
        protocols:
          http: { endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318 }
    processors:
      batch: {}
    exporters:
      otlphttp:
        endpoint: http://relay:4318
        retry_on_failure:
          max_interval: 5s
    service:
      telemetry:
        metrics:
          readers:
            - pull:
                exporter:
                  prometheus: { host: 0.0.0.0, port: 8888 }
      pipelines:
        traces:
          receivers: [otlp]
          processors: [batch]
          exporters: [otlphttp]
  migrated.yaml: |
    receivers:
      otlp:
        protocols:
          http: { endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318 }
    exporters:
      otlphttp:
        endpoint: http://relay:4318
        retry_on_failure:
          max_interval: 5s
        sending_queue:
          batch:
            enabled: true
    service:
      telemetry:
        metrics:
          readers:
            - pull:
                exporter:
                  prometheus: { host: 0.0.0.0, port: 8888 }
      pipelines:
        traces:
          receivers: [otlp]
          exporters: [otlphttp]
  sized.yaml: |
    receivers:
      otlp:
        protocols:
          http: { endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318 }
    exporters:
      otlphttp:
        endpoint: http://relay:4318
        retry_on_failure:
          max_interval: 5s
        sending_queue:
          sizer: items
          queue_size: 100000
          batch:
            enabled: true
    service:
      telemetry:
        metrics:
          readers:
            - pull:
                exporter:
                  prometheus: { host: 0.0.0.0, port: 8888 }
      pipelines:
        traces:
          receivers: [otlp]
          exporters: [otlphttp]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: demo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  strategy: { type: Recreate }
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: gateway }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: { app: gateway }
    spec:
      nodeName: APP_NODE
      enableServiceLinks: false
      containers:
        - name: otel
          image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.165.0
          args: ["--config=/conf/$(CONFIG)"]
          env:
            - { name: CONFIG, value: batch.yaml }
            - { name: LAB_RUN, value: "none" }
          ports:
            - containerPort: 4318
            - containerPort: 8888
          resources:
            requests: { cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi }
            limits: { memory: 1Gi }
          readinessProbe:
            tcpSocket: { port: 4318 }
            periodSeconds: 2
          volumeMounts:
            - { name: conf, mountPath: /conf }
      volumes:
        - name: conf
          configMap: { name: gateway }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: demo
spec:
  selector: { app: gateway }
  ports:
    - { name: otlp-http, port: 4318 }
    - { name: metrics, port: 8888 }
---
# The relay: the same Collector image, passing traces on to the Splunk agent on its node. It has no processors and keeps
# the exporter's defaults. Scaled to 0, it is the gateway's outage; scaled back to 1, the gateway drains its queue.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: relay
  namespace: demo
data:
  relay.yaml: |
    receivers:
      otlp:
        protocols:
          http: { endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318 }
    exporters:
      otlphttp:
        endpoint: http://${env:HOST_IP}:4318
    service:
      telemetry:
        metrics:
          readers:
            - pull:
                exporter:
                  prometheus: { host: 0.0.0.0, port: 8888 }
      pipelines:
        traces:
          receivers: [otlp]
          exporters: [otlphttp]
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: relay
  namespace: demo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels: { app: relay }
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: { app: relay }
    spec:
      nodeName: APP_NODE
      enableServiceLinks: false
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 5
      containers:
        - name: otel
          image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.165.0
          args: ["--config=/conf/relay.yaml"]
          env:
            - name: HOST_IP
              valueFrom: { fieldRef: { fieldPath: status.hostIP } }
          ports:
            - containerPort: 4318
            - containerPort: 8888
          resources:
            requests: { cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi }
            limits: { memory: 512Mi }
          readinessProbe:
            tcpSocket: { port: 4318 }
            periodSeconds: 2
          volumeMounts:
            - { name: conf, mountPath: /conf }
      volumes:
        - name: conf
          configMap: { name: relay }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: relay
  namespace: demo
spec:
  selector: { app: relay }
  ports:
    - { name: otlp-http, port: 4318 }
    - { name: metrics, port: 8888 }
---
# The gateway's and the relay's own metrics, read by the stats pod. `gwstats.py` prints the counts once; `gwstats.py watch N`
# prints the gateway's queue size, accepted and sent counts every 2 s, N times.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: stats
  namespace: demo
data:
  gwstats.py: |
    import re, sys, time, urllib.request
    def read(host):
        try:
            return urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://{host}:8888/metrics", timeout=5).read().decode()
        except Exception:
            return ""
    def total(text, name, **labels):
        t = 0.0
        for line in text.splitlines():
            m = re.match(r"^([a-zA-Z_:][\w:]*)(\{[^}]*\})?\s+([0-9.eE+-]+)", line)
            if not m or m[1] not in (name, name + "_total"):
                continue
            got = dict(re.findall(r'(\w+)="([^"]*)"', m[2] or ""))
            if all(got.get(k) == v for k, v in labels.items()):
                t += float(m[3])
        return t
    if sys.argv[1:2] == ["watch"]:
        for _ in range(int(sys.argv[2])):
            g = read("gateway")
            print(f"Q {time.time():.0f} size={total(g, 'otelcol_exporter_queue_size', exporter='otlphttp'):g} "
                  f"capacity={total(g, 'otelcol_exporter_queue_capacity', exporter='otlphttp'):g} up={1 if g else 0} "
                  f"accepted={total(g, 'otelcol_receiver_accepted_spans', receiver='otlp'):g} "
                  f"sent={total(g, 'otelcol_exporter_sent_spans', exporter='otlphttp'):g}", flush=True)
            time.sleep(2)
        sys.exit(0)
    g, r = read("gateway"), read("relay")
    rows = {
        "accepted": total(g, "otelcol_receiver_accepted_spans", receiver="otlp"),
        "refused": total(g, "otelcol_receiver_refused_spans", receiver="otlp"),
        "enqueue_failed": total(g, "otelcol_exporter_enqueue_failed_spans", exporter="otlphttp"),
        "sent": total(g, "otelcol_exporter_sent_spans", exporter="otlphttp"),
        "send_failed": total(g, "otelcol_exporter_send_failed_spans", exporter="otlphttp"),
        "queue_size": total(g, "otelcol_exporter_queue_size", exporter="otlphttp"),
        "queue_capacity": total(g, "otelcol_exporter_queue_capacity", exporter="otlphttp"),
        "relay_accepted": total(r, "otelcol_receiver_accepted_spans", receiver="otlp"),
    }
    for k, v in rows.items():
        print(f"GW {k}={v:g}")
    if g and not rows["accepted"]:
        print("GW metric names held: " + " ".join(sorted({l.split("{")[0].split(" ")[0] for l in g.splitlines() if l.startswith("otelcol_")}))[:900])
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: stats
  namespace: demo
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  nodeName: LOAD_NODE
  enableServiceLinks: false
  volumes:
    - name: stats
      configMap:
        name: stats
  containers:
    - name: stats
      image: python:3.12-slim
      command: ["sleep", "7200"]
      volumeMounts:
        - { name: stats, mountPath: /stats }
      resources:
        requests: { cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi }

# Shared by reproduce.sh and fix.sh. Sourced, never run alone.
# A run = a fresh gateway with one config, the relay up, 50 s of load at 60 single-span requests a second, and a 30 s
# outage (the relay scaled to 0) from 10 s to 40 s into the load. A watcher reads the gateway's queue size, accepted and
# sent counts every 2 s. seconds_to_drain = from the relay's scale-up to the first of 3 reads in a row whose queue size is
# back at or below its highest read before the outage. After the load, the final counts wait until the queue reads 0 and sent hasn't moved
# for 3 reads in a row (6 s, longer than the 5 s retry cap), for 60 s at most. Runs: batch-1/2, migrated-1/2, sized-1/2. Nothing else differs.
# runs.txt holds each run's window ("<run> <load start> <drain end>"), and runs are at least 30 s apart, so Splunk is
# read per run with no overlap.
export LC_ALL=C
OUTAGE_AFTER=10 OUTAGE_S=30 DRAIN_MAX=60 GAP=30

start_run() {   # run label, seconds allowed
  local cfg=${1%-*} last
  last=$(awk 'END {print $3}' runs.txt 2>/dev/null)
  kubectl -n demo scale deploy/relay --replicas=1 >/dev/null || fail "could not start the relay"
  kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/relay --timeout="$(cap "$2" 300)s" >/dev/null || { why relay; fail "the relay is not up"; }
  kubectl -n demo set env deployment/gateway "CONFIG=$cfg.yaml" "LAB_RUN=$1" >/dev/null || fail "could not set the gateway config"
  kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/gateway --timeout="$(cap "$2" 300)s" >/dev/null || { why gateway; fail "the gateway did not roll out"; }
  local g; g=$(newest gateway)
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do kubectl -n demo logs "$g" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'Everything is ready' && break; sleep 1; done
  echo "$1: gateway $(kubectl -n demo get "$g" -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].image}') --config=/conf/$cfg.yaml ($(kubectl -n demo logs "$g" 2>/dev/null | grep -c 'Everything is ready') ready line)"
  # Keep the previous run's drain and this run's load at least GAP seconds apart, so their Splunk windows can't overlap.
  if [ -n "$last" ]; then local w=$(( last + GAP - $(date +%s) )); [ "$w" -gt 0 ] && sleep "$w"; fi
  return 0
}

outage_run() {   # run label
  kubectl -n demo wait pod/stats --for=condition=Ready --timeout=60s >/dev/null || fail "the stats pod is not ready"
  kubectl -n demo delete pod load --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null 2>&1
  kubectl -n demo exec stats -- python /stats/gwstats.py > "gw-$1-start.txt" || fail "could not read the gateway's metrics"
  local t_load t_down t_up sent prev same q
  sed -e "s/LOAD_NODE/$LOAD_NODE/" -e "s/LAB_ENV/$LAB_NAME/" -e "s/lab.run=\"RUN\"/lab.run=\"$1\"/" k8s/20-load.yaml |
    kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not start the load"
  kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=condition=Ready --timeout=60s >/dev/null || { why gateway; fail "the load did not start"; }
  t_load=$(date +%s)
  timeout 200 kubectl -n demo exec stats -- python /stats/gwstats.py watch 60 > "q-$1.txt" 2>/dev/null &
  local watcher=$!
  sleep "$OUTAGE_AFTER"
  kubectl -n demo scale deploy/relay --replicas=0 >/dev/null || fail "could not stop the relay"
  t_down=$(date +%s)
  kubectl -n demo wait pod -l app=relay --for=delete --timeout=25s >/dev/null 2>&1
  echo "$1: relay scaled to 0 at +$(( t_down - t_load ))s; relay endpoints now: [$(kubectl -n demo get endpoints relay -o jsonpath='{.subsets[*].addresses[*].ip}' 2>/dev/null || true)]"
  local w=$(( OUTAGE_S - ($(date +%s) - t_down) )); [ "$w" -gt 0 ] && sleep "$w"
  kubectl -n demo scale deploy/relay --replicas=1 >/dev/null || fail "could not restart the relay"
  t_up=$(date +%s)
  kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/relay --timeout=60s >/dev/null || { why relay; fail "the relay did not come back"; }
  echo "$1: relay scaled to 1 at +$(( t_up - t_load ))s, ready at +$(( $(date +%s) - t_load ))s (outage $(( t_up - t_down ))s)"
  kubectl -n demo wait pod/load --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Succeeded --timeout=60s >/dev/null || { kubectl -n demo logs load --tail=10; fail "the load did not finish"; }
  kubectl -n demo logs load > "load-$1.txt" 2>/dev/null
  prev=-1 same=0
  for i in $(seq 1 $(( DRAIN_MAX / 2 ))); do
    kubectl -n demo exec stats -- python /stats/gwstats.py > "gw-$1-now.txt" 2>/dev/null
    q=$(sed -n 's/^GW queue_size=//p' "gw-$1-now.txt"); sent=$(sed -n 's/^GW sent=//p' "gw-$1-now.txt")
    if [ "${q:-1}" = 0 ] && [ "${sent:-x}" = "$prev" ]; then same=$(( same + 1 )); else same=0; fi
    prev=${sent:--1}
    [ "$same" -ge 2 ] && break
    sleep 2
  done
  # Complete only when the queue is empty, sent has stopped moving, and sent covers everything accepted that the exporter
  # took (with the batch processor, spans that failed to enqueue were accepted first; without it they were refused).
  drain_complete=0
  local a e
  a=$(sed -n 's/^GW accepted=//p' "gw-$1-now.txt"); e=$(sed -n 's/^GW enqueue_failed=//p' "gw-$1-now.txt")
  [ "$same" -ge 2 ] && awk -v s="${sent:-0}" -v a="${a:-0}" -v e="${e:-0}" 'BEGIN { exit !(s + 0 >= a - e) }' && drain_complete=1
  [ "$drain_complete" = 1 ] || echo "$1: drain incomplete after ${DRAIN_MAX}s (queue ${q:-?}, sent ${sent:-?}, accepted ${a:-?}, enqueue failed ${e:-?}); sent and lost below are as read then"
  kubectl -n demo exec stats -- python /stats/gwstats.py > "gw-$1-end.txt" || fail "could not read the gateway's metrics"
  kill "$watcher" 2>/dev/null; wait "$watcher" 2>/dev/null
  echo "$1 $t_load $(date +%s) $t_down $t_up" >> runs.txt
}

gwd() {   # run label, count name: end minus start
  local a b; a=$(sed -n "s/^GW $2=//p" "gw-$1-start.txt"); b=$(sed -n "s/^GW $2=//p" "gw-$1-end.txt")
  awk -v a="${a:-0}" -v b="${b:-0}" 'BEGIN { printf "%.0f", b - a }'
}

traces() {   # run label: traces the load's 4 workers say they generated
  grep 'traces generated' "load-$1.txt" | grep -oE '"traces": ?[0-9]+|traces=[0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+$' | awk '{t += $1} END {printf "%.0f", t}'
}

# From the watcher's 2 s reads: accepted spans a second between 2 s and 10 s into the load (before the outage), the
# highest queue size before the outage, and seconds from the relay's return (its scale-up command, so the relay's rollout
# is included) until the queue is back at or below that level and stays there for 3 reads in a row.
watch_figures() {   # run label. Sets rate, pre_peak, drained.
  local t_load t_down t_up
  read -r _ t_load _ t_down t_up < <(awk -v r="$1" '$1 == r' runs.txt)
  read -r rate pre_peak drained < <(awk -v l="$t_load" -v d="$t_down" -v u="$t_up" '
    { t = $2; for (i = 3; i <= NF; i++) { split($i, kv, "="); v[kv[1]] = kv[2] + 0 }
      if (t >= l + 2 && a0 == "") { a0 = v["accepted"]; t0 = t }
      if (t <= l + 10) { a1 = v["accepted"]; t1 = t }
      if (t < d && v["size"] > pp) pp = v["size"]
      if (t >= u && dr == "") { if (v["size"] <= pp + 0) { if (++low == 1) first = t; if (low >= 3) dr = first - u } else low = 0 } }
    END { r = (t1 > t0) ? (a1 - a0) / (t1 - t0) : 0; printf "%.1f %.0f %s\n", r, pp + 0, (dr == "" ? -1 : dr) }' "q-$1.txt")
}

measures() {   # run label: the sender's count, the gateway's counts, and its queue during the run
  local gen tr acc ref enq sent sfail lost peak capa workers
  tr=$(traces "$1"); gen=$(( ${tr:-0} * 2 )); workers=$(grep -c 'traces generated' "load-$1.txt")
  watch_figures "$1"
  acc=$(gwd "$1" accepted); ref=$(gwd "$1" refused); enq=$(gwd "$1" enqueue_failed); sent=$(gwd "$1" sent)
  sfail=$(gwd "$1" send_failed); lost=$(( ${gen:-0} - sent ))
  peak=$(awk '{sub("size=", "", $3); if ($3 + 0 > m) m = $3 + 0} END {printf "%.0f", m}' "q-$1.txt")
  capa=$(awk '{sub("capacity=", "", $4); if ($4 + 0 > m) m = $4 + 0} END {printf "%.0f", m}' "q-$1.txt")
  echo "$1 gateway counters at start: $(tr '\n' ' ' < "gw-$1-start.txt")"
  echo "$1 gateway counters at end:   $(tr '\n' ' ' < "gw-$1-end.txt")"
  echo "$1 load log: $(grep -E 'traces generated|limited' "load-$1.txt" | cut -c1-160 | tr '\n' ' ')"
  echo "$1 queue reads: $(wc -l < "q-$1.txt"), highest size $peak of $capa (before the outage: $pre_peak); accepted $rate spans/s from 2 s to 10 s into the load"
  echo "$1: the load generated $tr traces = $gen spans ($workers workers reported, 2 spans a trace); the gateway accepted $acc, refused $ref attempts, failed to enqueue $enq, sent $sent; export attempts failed $sfail; generated but never sent $lost; queue back to its pre-outage level ${drained}s after the relay returned (-1: not within the reads)"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: load_spans_generated[$1]=${gen:-0}"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: gateway_spans_accepted[$1]=$acc"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: gateway_accept_rate[$1]=$rate"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: gateway_spans_refused[$1]=$ref"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: gateway_enqueue_failed[$1]=$enq"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: gateway_spans_sent[$1]=$sent"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: spans_lost[$1]=$lost"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: queue_peak[$1]=$peak"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: seconds_to_drain[$1]=$drained"
  echo "HERO_MEASURE: drain_complete[$1]=$drain_complete"
  echo "$1 ${gen:-0} $acc $ref $enq $sent $lost $peak $capa $drained $rate $drain_complete" >> results.txt
  [ "$workers" = 4 ] || fail "$1: $workers of 4 load workers reported a count, so the sender's total isn't known"
  [ "$acc" -gt 0 ] || fail "the gateway accepted no spans in $1"
  [ "$sfail" -gt 0 ] || [ "$enq" -gt 0 ] || [ "$ref" -gt 0 ] || echo "note: $1 saw no failed export attempt, so the outage may not have reached the gateway"
}

col() { awk -v r="$1" -v c="$2" '$1 == r {print $c}' results.txt; }   # run, column: 2 generated, 5 enqueue failed, 7 lost
summary() {
  printf '%-11s %9s %7s %9s %8s %9s %8s %6s %7s %9s %8s %9s\n' run generated rate/s accepted refused enq_fail sent lost peak capacity drain_s complete
  while read -r r a b c d e f g h i j k; do printf '%-11s %9s %7s %9s %8s %9s %8s %6s %7s %9s %8s %9s\n' "$r" "$a" "$j" "$b" "$c" "$d" "$e" "$f" "$g" "$h" "$i" "$k"; done < results.txt
  echo "(refused counts attempts: the sender may retry a refused request. lost = generated by the sender - sent by the gateway.)"
}

# Sums every point SignalFlow returns between start and stop (10 s resolution), across all series.
sf_total() {   # program, start s, stop s. Read up to 3 times if the stream comes back empty.
  local out n
  for try in 1 2 3; do
    out=$(signalflow "$1" "$(( $2 * 1000 ))" "$(( $3 * 1000 ))")
    [ -n "$out" ] && break
    sleep 5
  done
  n=$(awk '{t += $2} END {printf "%.0f", t}' <<<"$out")
  echo "${n:-0}"
}

# Spans Splunk APM counts for the load service from a run's load start to 20 s after its drain, in whole 10 s points.
apm_spans() {   # run label
  local s e f n
  s=$(awk -v r="$1" '$1 == r {print $2}' runs.txt); e=$(awk -v r="$1" '$1 == r {print $3}' runs.txt)
  s=$(( s / 10 * 10 )); e=$(( (e + 20 + 9) / 10 * 10 ))
  f="filter('sf_environment', '$LAB_NAME') and filter('sf_service', 'checkout-load')"
  n=$(sf_total "data('spans.count', filter=$f, rollup='delta').sum().publish()" "$s" "$e")
  # Orgs on histogram MetricSets hold the count as histogram('spans'), so that form is read too when the first is empty.
  [ "$n" = 0 ] && n=$(sf_total "histogram('spans', filter=$f).count().publish()" "$s" "$e")
  echo "$n"
}

# Generic helpers: the clock and pods.
start_clock() {   # seconds allowed, the result to print on failure. Every wait is capped so a result always prints.
  START=$(date +%s); LIMIT=$1; FAILED=$2; HERO_DONE=0
  trap '[ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $FAILED"; }' EXIT
}
remaining() { echo $(( START + LIMIT - $(date +%s) )); }
cap() { local want=$1 reserve=$2 r; r=$(( $(remaining) - reserve )); [ "$r" -lt 5 ] && r=5; [ "$want" -lt "$r" ] && echo "$want" || echo "$r"; }
emit() { HERO_DONE=1; echo "HERO_RESULT: $1"; }
fail() { echo "FAIL: $*"; [ "$HERO_DONE" = 1 ] || emit "$FAILED"; exit 0; }

newest() { kubectl -n demo get pods -l "app=$1" --field-selector=status.phase=Running --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp -o name | tail -1; }
why() { kubectl -n demo get pods -o wide | tail -8; kubectl -n demo get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -8 | cut -c1-180; kubectl -n demo logs deploy/"$1" --tail=20 2>/dev/null | cut -c1-200; }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# BEFORE and the problem. The gateway Collector takes 60 single-span requests a second, and its export target (the relay)
# goes away for 30 s. batch-1 and batch-2 run the batch processor with its defaults and the default sending_queue. Then
# migrated-1 and migrated-2 make the one-line migration from the OpenTelemetry blog: no batch processor, sending_queue batch
# enabled, the queue left at its defaults. Every count comes from the gateway's own metrics.
# Reproduced when the exporter fails to enqueue spans in both migrated runs and in neither batch run. Refused attempts and
# spans lost (generated by the sender, never sent by the gateway) are printed per run. fix.sh sizes the queue in items.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
. ./lib.sh

start_clock 820 not_reproduced

aws eks update-kubeconfig --name "$(terraform output -raw cluster_name)" --region "$AWS_REGION" >/dev/null || fail "could not write kubeconfig"
for v in SPLUNK_REALM SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN SPLUNK_API_TOKEN; do [ -n "${!v:-}" ] || fail "$v is not set"; done

echo "== 1. Waiting for 2 worker nodes"
ready=0
t0=$(date +%s)
while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt 300 ]; do
  ready=$(kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes --no-headers 2>/dev/null | grep -c ' Ready' || true)
  [ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] && break
  sleep 10
done
kubectl --request-timeout=15s get nodes --no-headers -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,TYPE:.metadata.labels.node\.kubernetes\.io/instance-type,READY:.status.conditions[-1].type || true
[ "${ready:-0}" -ge 2 ] || fail "nodes did not become Ready"
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deploy/coredns --timeout="$(cap 90 600)s" >/dev/null || true

# The gateway and the relay stay on one node, the load and the stats pod on the other, in every run.
APP_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
LOAD_NODE=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[1].metadata.name}')
echo "$APP_NODE" > app-node.txt
echo "$LOAD_NODE" > load-node.txt
echo "app node: $APP_NODE; load node: $LOAD_NODE"

echo "== 2. Installing the Splunk OTel Collector (chart 0.163.1), the same in every run"
for i in 1 2 3; do
  helm repo add splunk-otel-collector-chart https://signalfx.github.io/splunk-otel-collector-chart >/dev/null 2>&1 && helm repo update >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 10
done
helm upgrade --install splunk-otel-collector splunk-otel-collector-chart/splunk-otel-collector \
  --version 0.163.1 --namespace splunk --create-namespace \
  --set splunkObservability.realm="$SPLUNK_REALM" \
  --set splunkObservability.accessToken="$SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  --set clusterName="$LAB_NAME" \
  --set cloudProvider=aws \
  --set distribution=eks \
  >/dev/null || fail "collector install failed"
kubectl -n splunk rollout status daemonset/splunk-otel-collector-agent --timeout="$(cap 150 560)s" >/dev/null || fail "collector agent not ready"
echo "collector agent ready on $(kubectl -n splunk get daemonset splunk-otel-collector-agent -o jsonpath='{.status.numberReady}') nodes"

echo "== 3. Deploying the gateway and the relay (contrib 0.165.0) and the stats pod"
kubectl create namespace demo --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null
sed -e "s/APP_NODE/$APP_NODE/" -e "s/LOAD_NODE/$LOAD_NODE/" k8s/30-gateway.yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null || fail "could not deploy the gateway"
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/relay --timeout="$(cap 120 520)s" >/dev/null || { why relay; fail "the relay did not start"; }
kubectl -n demo rollout status deploy/gateway --timeout="$(cap 120 510)s" >/dev/null || { why gateway; fail "the gateway did not start"; }
kubectl -n demo wait pod/stats --for=condition=Ready --timeout="$(cap 120 500)s" >/dev/null || fail "the stats pod is not ready"
echo "effective gateway configs:"
kubectl -n demo get configmap gateway -o jsonpath='{.data.batch\.yaml}' | sed -n '/^processors/,/^service/p' | sed 's/^/  batch.yaml    | /'
kubectl -n demo get configmap gateway -o jsonpath='{.data.migrated\.yaml}' | sed -n '/^exporters/,/^service/p' | sed 's/^/  migrated.yaml | /'

rm -f runs.txt results.txt
for r in batch-1 migrated-1 batch-2 migrated-2; do
  echo "== Run $r: ${r%-*}.yaml, 50 s of load, the relay down from 10 s to 40 s"
  start_run "$r" 120
  outage_run "$r"
  measures "$r"
done

echo "== Summary"
summary

ok=1
for r in batch-1 batch-2; do [ "$(col "$r" 5)" = 0 ] || ok=0; done
for r in migrated-1 migrated-2; do [ "$(col "$r" 5)" -gt 0 ] || ok=0; done
[ "$ok" = 1 ] && emit reproduced || emit not_reproduced

# Low-level Splunk Observability Cloud reads used by lib.sh: series, traces from APM by trace ID, and SignalFlow sums.
# Sourced, never run alone. Needs SPLUNK_REALM and SPLUNK_API_TOKEN.
API="https://api.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
STREAM="https://stream.${SPLUNK_REALM}.signalfx.com"
series() { curl -sS --max-time 20 -G -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/metrictimeseries" --data-urlencode "query=$1" --data-urlencode "limit=1000" 2>/dev/null; }

wait_cluster() {   # seconds. Sets cluster to how many of the cluster's series Splunk holds.
  local t0; t0=$(date +%s); cluster=0
  while [ $(( $(date +%s) - t0 )) -lt "$1" ]; do
    cluster=$(series "k8s.cluster.name:${LAB_NAME}" | jq -r '.count // (.results | length) // 0' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    [ "${cluster:-0}" -gt 0 ] && break
    sleep 15
  done
}

trace_items() {   # every span Splunk APM holds for a trace: the newest segment, then each segment
  local seg
  {
    curl -sS --max-time 20 -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/apm/trace/$1/latest" 2>/dev/null | jq -c 'if type == "array" then . else [] end' 2>/dev/null
    for seg in $(curl -sS --max-time 20 -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/apm/trace/$1/segments" 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'if type == "array" then .[] else empty end' 2>/dev/null); do
      curl -sS --max-time 20 -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" "$API/v2/apm/trace/$1/$seg" 2>/dev/null | jq -c 'if type == "array" then . else [] end' 2>/dev/null
    done
  } | jq -cs 'add // [] | unique_by(.spanId // .id // tostring)' 2>/dev/null
}

# SignalFlow answers as a stream of events. This prints one value per point between start and stop, summed across series.
signalflow() {   # program, start ms, stop ms, resolution ms
  curl -sS --max-time 60 -X POST -H "X-SF-Token: $SPLUNK_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: text/plain" --data-binary "$1" \
    "$STREAM/v2/signalflow/execute?start=$2&stop=$3&resolution=${4:-10000}&immediate=true" 2>/dev/null |
    awk '/^event:/ { if (b != "") print e "\t" b; e = $2; b = ""; next }
         /^data:/  { sub(/^data: ?/, ""); b = b $0; next }
         END       { if (b != "") print e "\t" b }' |
    jq -Rr --argjson from "$2" --argjson to "$3" 'split("\t") | select(.[0] == "data") | (.[1] | fromjson? // {})
      | select(.logicalTimestampMs >= $from and .logicalTimestampMs < $to) | "\(.logicalTimestampMs) \([.data[]?.value // empty] | add // 0)"' 2>/dev/null
}
